test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 16 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: If the manufacturer gains 10%, the wholesaler gains 15%, and the retailer gains 28%, then find the cost of production of a table (in ₹), whose retail price for the customer is ₹75,900. (NOTE: Manufacturer sells to wholesaler, wholesaler sells to retailer and retailer sells to customers.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the **cost of production** be x.

Retail Price = Cost × (1 + g₁%) × (1 + g₂%) × (1 + g₃%)

75,900 = x × (110 ÷ 100) × (115 ÷ 100) × (128 ÷ 100)

75,900 = x × (11 ÷ 10) × (23 ÷ 20) × (32 ÷ 25)

x = (75,900 × 10 × 20 × 25) ÷ (11 × 23 × 32)

**∴ The correct answer is ₹46,875.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Manufacturer Gain = 10%, Wholesaler Gain = 15%, Retailer Gain = 28%, Retail Price = ₹75,900.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + Gain%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93f020ead27336c61ab52442380f23b7dc5a9b419744c2309ccec96d0e294f77.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost of Production** be CP.

⇒ Price for Wholesaler = CP × 1.10

⇒ Price for Retailer = (CP × 1.10) × 1.15

⇒ Price for Customer = (CP × 1.10 × 1.15) × 1.28 = 75,900

⇒ CP × 1.6192 = 75,900

⇒ CP = 75,900 ÷ 1.6192 = 46,875

**∴ The correct answer is ₹46,875.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value changes multiple times in sequence, the net multiplier is the product of individual multipliers: Mₙₑₜ = (1 + r₁) × (1 + r₂) × ... × (1 + rₙ).

Effective Profit Percentage

In a chain of transactions, the final price is calculated by applying each **profit margin** consecutively on the preceding value.
